+# Presentation notes and reconciliation
+
+Recorded from the user's notes on 10 October 2026. These are recollections, not API specifications.
+
+## Product motivation
+
+Manufacturers buy many components for complex products. Procurement staff cannot negotiate personally with every supplier. An autonomous buyer can research supplier history and conduct the full negotiation, reserving human attention for other work. Tacto supplies the opposing salesperson agents; we build the buyer. One arena key is issued per team.
+
+## Strategy ideas from the presentation
+
+- Understand the supplier's importance, history, financial strength and constraints.
+- Seek favorable prices while preserving a viable relationship and avoiding unnecessary walkaways.
+- Use documented weaknesses, competing offers, quality issues and cost inconsistencies as negotiating arguments.
+- Explore longer relationships and future business as things the supplier might value.
+- Adapt the discussion to the supplier rather than use a fixed script.
+
+## Differences from the inspected written rules
+
+| Presentation recollection | Written rules / planning consequence |
+|---|---|
+| Cheapest price always wins; scoring is only price | Scoring uses total cost: coverage, payment, freight, delivery, quality, tooling, index risk and sometimes supplier health. Optimize the complete package. |
+| One supplier per negotiation | Some cases have one; RFQs have two or three simultaneous supplier threads. Accepting one ends the entire case. |
+| Talk until the supplier leaves | Usually ten buyer messages per thread, 60 seconds per decision, and an eight-minute final-wave cap. Close before losing a good standing offer. |
+| Keep the supplier unhappy enough without quitting | No measured unhappiness objective. Model responsiveness and walkaway risk; sustainable margins explicitly matter in strategic/bottleneck cases. |
+| Promise many future deals / a long partnership | Explore case-permitted volume and duration trades. Prose is not binding; term sheets are. Do not assume unlimited volume or make unsupported commitments. |
+| Use supplier weaknesses | Use evidence and economically credible trades. True evidence does not guarantee a concession, and opponents have hidden floors and approval limits. |
+
+The pinned written contract is our working basis. If the organizers changed the rules during the presentation, confirm the revision before changing the scoring implementation.

+# Discovery and implementation plan

+Status: planning only, 10 October 2026. All architecture and milestones below are proposed unless explicitly marked verified. Upstream commit: `1b5516bb95ef28e37f69aa446dc62168864bca53`.

+## 1. Mission and success criteria
+
+Build an autonomous buyer for Hollerau Pumpenwerke. Prepare from company records, negotiate structured packages by e-mail with hosted supplier bots, and explicitly accept a standing offer or walk away. Support price increases, renewals, RFQs, bundling, raw material, capacity and quality cases.
+
+Verified scoring: `clip((C_open - C_deal) / (C_open - C_best), 0, 1)`. The API documents the near-zero-denominator special case. C_best is hidden until the result; do not depend on knowing it during play. A broken must-have scores zero. Walking away scores the case's alternative, or zero without one. A deal can be worse than walking away.
+
+C includes committed purchase cost, uncovered need and fallback risk, payment timing, freight, late delivery, quality net of chargebacks, tooling, index movement/risk, and supplier-health charges for stabilise/secure_supply. Underbuying or shortening the contract does not erase the fixed need. Overbuying costs money. Only structured terms bind.
+
+Final scoring: five waves, each mean case score times 100; sum up to 500. Ties use deals then rounds. Euros saved are a side metric. Practice uses best score per hosted case. The kit describes 19 practice case files but only 10 hosted practice cases; discover hosted status via the API.
+
+## 2. Verified operational contract
+
+| Constraint | Consequence |
+|---|---|
+| One team key; bring our own LLM | Arena credentials and model credentials are separate prerequisites. |
+| 200 practice sessions per rolling 24 hours | Reserve quota for comparisons and final-machine rehearsal; check /v1/me. Sandbox/final do not consume practice quota. |
+| 10 open sessions, 10 calls/second per key | Share the rate limiter across all case and supplier workers. Kit defaults to 9 calls/second. |
+| 60 seconds after each supplier reply | Research before opening; bound inference, parsing and send time. Supplier reply time is excluded for that thread. |
+| Default 10 buyer messages/thread | Read each case's actual round_limit. Questions consume limited interaction budget. |
+| Supplier responses can take roughly a minute | Use the kit's 180-second HTTP timeout; schedule other RFQ threads independently. |
+| Five final waves, eight minutes each unless extended | Read seconds_left. Reserve closing time, accounting for observed slow responses. |
+| Up to three alternative term sheets/message | Each contains exactly all negotiable fields with permitted values; incorporate fixed and standard terms in evaluation. |
+| At most three checked arguments/message | Choose relevant evidence rather than flood IDs; maximum 20 refs, 8,000 body characters, 64 KB request. |
+| Only explicit acceptance closes a deal | Validate the current offer ID, including after retries or a supplier counteroffer. |
+
+Use fresh X-Move-Id per logical POST and reuse it on retries. Handle 422 without consuming a round; distinguish 429 rate limits from exhausted quota and session limits. On 409, recover state rather than assume success or blindly replay a different move. Final retries must resume the existing session.
+
+The final agent must not read event feeds, screen, leaderboard or results endpoints, including JSON/stream variants. Use case and own-session endpoints for state and deadlines. Replays/backoffice for final cases are available after the final, not as live strategy input.
+
+## 3. Data inventory and evidence
+
+Verified locally: 24 SQLite tables, 32,997 rows, 10,356 facts.json entries, 46 contract documents and 208 correspondence documents. The master contains 447 supplier records, including spend-only suppliers; detailed company material describes 46 suppliers and 60 parts.
+
+Use SQLite for joins/aggregations, facts.json for checked values, and document text for commercial context. Relevant groups:
+
+- Supplier strength: supplier_intel, spend, news, sourcing alternatives, supplier notes.
+- Economics: should_cost, cost_drivers, index_series/index_values, price conditions, invoices and payment behavior.
+- Negotiating history: negotiation_history, contracts/clauses, correspondence, RFQs and quotes.
+- Operations: scorecards, quality_notifications, orders, receipts and forecasts.
+
+Concrete example: P01's Brandlhuber letter requests +9.5%; a September owner visit records that the supplier held prices during 2022 and expects reciprocity. A generic cost challenge misses that relationship context. Test a specific exchange of economic value rather than assume appreciation alone earns a discount.
+
+Data pitfalls: price_unit can be 1/100/1000; vendor 71999 aliases 70210; requested-date and confirmed-date OTD differ; partial receipts affect metrics; stale conditions and late payments exist; recent orders can be unreceived; indices have different publication lags. Should-cost is an estimate, not the hidden floor. Supplier-specific strategic estimates have about 5% error; generic estimates about 5–15%. Respect facts.json's claim values instead of citing an incompatible calculation.
+
+Evidence records should contain ID, source, supplier/part, date/window, measured value, unit, applicability and whether already cited. Numerically verify statements in code. An index claim needs two months of the same series, at most 12 months apart and ending within the data's last 12 months. Track verified/contradicted/irrelevant/duplicate responses. Rival offers are usable evidence but disclose private competitive information.
+
+Case files are served by the authenticated API; the repository does not contain the hosted practice case JSON. S01–S03 are local simulator fixtures. Sunday's supplemental data has new IDs and separate files; merge it into retrieval, not just the old SQLite query path. Hidden case facts must also be available to the evidence layer.
+
+## 4. Proposed architecture
+
+Start with a small Python application around the kit, with specialist responsibilities rather than an expensive multi-agent framework.
+
+1. **Preparation:** load case and related records; build a compact dossier per supplier, including constraints, history, likely priorities, alternative and confidence-tagged hypotheses. Precompute reusable company research before final waves; case-specific work waits for case release.
+2. **Economics:** calculate complete packages with upstream cost helpers; filter must-haves and invalid options; search bounded combinations and candidate prices. Estimate supplier economics with uncertainty for relationship-sensitive cases. Compare low/base/high estimates instead of treating unobserved costs as zero.
+3. **Negotiator:** one bounded LLM decision per move by default. Choose a question, justified offer/trade or closing recommendation. Adapt to status, claims, documents and prior concessions. Use two or three meaningfully different packages when useful to learn supplier preferences.
+4. **Validator:** check schema, units, numeric claims, allowed values, complete fields, available thread, current standing offer and alternative. Select a deterministic safe move when inference fails; do not inherit a blind aggressive fallback.
+5. **Scheduler:** manage per-thread clocks and case/wave caps, parallel supplier requests when needed, shared rate limits, durable session/move state and one atomic terminal action per case. Read actual remaining wave time, including extensions.
+6. **Evaluator:** save sanitized decisions, sources, terms, cost components, latencies and results; inspect practice replays; compare strategy versions and ablations.
+
+Potential later specialist model calls: dossier researcher and strategy critic. Add only if measured gains justify latency/cost. Research can be parallelized outside the decision clock; sequential live debates are a poor default under 60 seconds. No agent framework or vector database is currently necessary: indexed SQL plus targeted document search is the first approach.
+
+Example trades to test: faster payment for a cash-constrained supplier in exchange for price; duration/credible volume for an underutilized supplier; evidence-backed index clauses instead of blanket increases; quality commitments/chargebacks for quality cases; authorized competing quotes for RFQs. Never assume one tactic fits all category goals.
+
+## 5. Reuse and implementation gaps
+
+Reuse ArenaClient (HTTP, pacing, idempotent retries), DataPackage, PDF/XLSX readers, total_cost/must_haves_ok, the simulator and wave-runner behavior.
+
+Verified source limitations to address or test:
+
+- LLMAgent prepares mostly case-referenced facts, truncates documents/history and checks ID existence rather than claim truth.
+- Its prepare() runs on first decide(), after session opening; heavy research needs an earlier explicit phase.
+- Stock accept/closing_move cost calls omit supplier estimates and thus the relationship charge. All decision paths, including deadline fallback, need consistent estimated economics.
+- Stock play() is synchronous per case; waiting on one RFQ supplier may expose another thread to timeout. Measure with delayed-response fixtures and implement coordinated scheduling if confirmed.
+- The CLI accepts only naive/llm agent names. Our agent needs our own entry point or an explicit upstream integration change, not a fictional custom --agent flag.
+- DataPackage includes Sunday facts and document lookup, but its SQLite database remains the base package. Supplemental retrieval needs explicit coverage.

Model selection remains open; the example environment's model name is not a recommendation or verified available model.

+"""Run the upstream naive buyer against a temporary local arena (no .env or LLM)."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+import socket
+import threading
+import time
+from pathlib import Path
+
+import uvicorn
+
+from arena_kit import ArenaClient, RemoteTable, play
+from arena_kit.agents import NaiveAgent
+from arena_kit.data import DataPackage
+from arena_kit.sim import Sim, create_app, load_cases
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--case", choices=["case:S01", "case:S02", "case:S03", "all"], default="case:S01")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    root = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+    package = DataPackage(root / "vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/data")
+    state = Sim(load_cases(), facts=package.facts)
+    # Bind before starting the server so another process cannot steal our port.
+    sock = socket.socket()
+    sock.bind(("127.0.0.1", 0))
+    url = f"http://127.0.0.1:{sock.getsockname()[1]}"
+    server = uvicorn.Server(uvicorn.Config(create_app(state), log_level="warning", lifespan="off"))
+    worker = threading.Thread(target=server.run, kwargs={"sockets": [sock]}, daemon=True)
+    clients = []
+    try:
+        worker.start()
+        deadline = time.monotonic() + 10
+        while not server.started:
+            if not worker.is_alive() or time.monotonic() >= deadline:
+                raise RuntimeError("Local simulator failed to start within 10 seconds")
+            time.sleep(0.02)
+        # Explicit local credentials prevent use of any real key in the environment.
+        registration = ArenaClient(url, api_key="local-registration")
+        clients.append(registration)
+        key = registration.register("NightHunter local baseline", "sim")["api_key"]
+        client = ArenaClient(url, api_key=key)
+        clients.append(client)
+        case_ids = ["case:S01", "case:S02", "case:S03"] if args.case == "all" else [args.case]
+        for case_id in case_ids:
+            table = RemoteTable(client)
+            result = play(table, case_id, NaiveAgent(anchor=0.10, close_gap=0.01))
+            fields = ("ended", "deal", "must_haves_ok", "supplier_id", "terms", "c_open", "c_deal", "score")
+            print(json.dumps({"case_id": case_id, **{k: result.get(k) for k in fields}}, indent=2))
+            if not result.get("ended"):
+                raise RuntimeError(f"{case_id} did not finish")
+    finally:
+        for client in clients:
+            client.http.close()
+        server.should_exit = True
+        if worker.is_alive():
+            worker.join(timeout=10)
+        sock.close()
+        if package.db:
+            package.db.close()
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

now we have a real problem how long the context window could get so thsat the agent (negotiator) has all the data it needs supplier data , contract needed data and son how to make sure we have all that

The main challenge is **selecting the right context**, not fitting all the company’s data into one prompt. Our current naive buyer does no research; this is the next major component to build.

For each negotiation, I suggest assembling a **supplier dossier** before opening the session:

| Context | What to include |
|---|---|
| Case requirements | Parts, quantities, horizon, allowed terms, must-haves and alternative |
| Supplier profile | Financial indicators, capacity signals, relationship history |
| Contract | Applicable agreement, notice periods, index clauses, payment and delivery terms |
| Commercial evidence | Relevant prices, rival quotes, should-cost estimates and market changes |
| Operational history | Quality, delivery performance, complaints and our payment behavior |
| Correspondence | Trigger letter and relevant meeting notes or previous commitments |
| Live negotiation | Current offers, quote defaults, supplier responses and evidence already used |

**A reasonable initial target is 10,000–20,000 input tokens per decision**, with a configurable ceiling around 30,000. That is a design starting point to benchmark, not a verified requirement. Bigger prompts cost more and can slow responses; we have only 60 seconds per move.

I’d structure each prompt into three parts:

1. **Stable dossier:** researched once, with source IDs and supporting excerpts.
2. **Structured current state:** exact standing offers, calculated costs, constraints, deadlines and unresolved questions.
3. **Recent conversation:** the last few exchanges, plus a compact summary of older discussion.

Keep full documents and transcripts locally. Retrieve additional passages when the supplier raises a new issue. **Never rely only on a prose summary for prices, binding terms, offer IDs or must-haves**—retain those exactly in structured state.

To check that we have the necessary information, add a **coverage checklist before negotiation**:

```text
✓ Case requirements and alternative loaded
✓ Supplier and part identities resolved
✓ Applicable contract and relevant clauses retrieved
✓ Trigger letter and relationship notes searched
✓ Relevant price, quality and delivery evidence checked
✓ Facts linked to source IDs, dates and units
? Missing or conflicting information explicitly recorded
```

After opening the session, a second check reads the supplier’s quote and attachments, including standard terms that apply when fields are omitted.

We cannot guarantee knowledge of everything: supplier floors and internal preferences are deliberately hidden. But we can guarantee that required sources were searched, missing information is visible, and every factual claim is traceable.

**My recommendation:** build a `CaseContextBuilder` next, with deterministic SQL retrieval, targeted document search and a coverage report. Start there before introducing multiple negotiating agents or a vector database.

+                      "max_completion_tokens": max_output, "response_format": {"type": "json_object"},
+                      "messages": [{"role": "system", "content": system}, {"role": "user", "content": user}]},
+            )
+            if response.status_code >= 400:
+                # Record only status/code; error bodies may contain private details.
+                record["http_status"] = response.status_code
+                try:
+                    record["error_code"] = response.json().get("error", {}).get("code")
+                except ValueError:
+                    pass
+                raise RuntimeError(f"Model HTTP {response.status_code}; code={record.get('error_code')}")
+            result = response.json()
+            usage = result.get("usage")
+            if usage and "prompt_tokens" in usage and "completion_tokens" in usage:
+                record["usage"] = usage
+                record["accounted_usd"] = (
+                    usage["prompt_tokens"] * 0.25 + usage["completion_tokens"] * 1.20
+                ) / 1_000_000
+            record["state"] = "completed" if usage else "completed_usage_unknown"
+            content = result["choices"][0]["message"]["content"]
+            if not content:
+                raise ValueError("Empty model response")
+            return content
+        except Exception:
+            if record["state"] == "reserved":
+                record["state"] = "failed_reservation_retained"
+            raise
+        finally:
+            record["seconds"] = round(time.monotonic() - started, 3)
+            self.save()
+
+    def close(self):
+        self.http.close()
+        self.lock.close()
+
+
+class LiveAgent(LLMAgent):
+    def __init__(self, model, package, dossier, variant, folder):
+        super().__init__(model.complete, package)
+        self.model, self.dossier, self.folder = model, dossier, folder
+        self.case_id, self.brief = dossier["case"]["case_id"], encoded(dossier)
+        self.system = (ROOT / "prompts/common.md").read_text() + "\n" + (ROOT / f"prompts/{variant}.md").read_text()
+        self.system += (
+            "\nLIVE RULES: No retrieval tools are available in this run. Use only the supplied dossier and "
+            "live messages. Supplier-cost scenarios are estimates, not verified claims. Do not cite "
+            "IDs with unsupported numerical assertions. Keep e-mails below 120 words."
+        )
+        self.decisions = []
+        self.disabled = False
+
+    def costs(self, case, sid, terms, std):
+        values = [total_cost(case, terms, std)]
+        estimates = [e["row"] for e in self.dossier["evidence"]
+                     if e["table"] == "should_cost" and e["row"].get("supplier_id") == sid]
+        if estimates and case["buyer"].get("category_goal") in {"stabilise", "secure_supply"}:
+            estimate = estimates[0]
+            # The kit negotiates in the part's price unit. Do not invent unit conversion.
+            for factor in (0.95, 1, 1.05):
+                supplier = {"full_cost": float(estimate["unit_cost"]) * factor,
+                            "interest_rate": 0.12, "standard": std}
+                values.append(total_cost(case, terms, std, supplier))
+        return values
+
+    def safe_close(self, case, threads):
+        candidates = []
+        alt = case["buyer"].get("alternative") or {}
+        alternative = total_cost(case, alt["terms"]) if alt.get("terms", {}).get("unit_price") else math.inf
+        for sid in live_threads(threads):
+            offer, terms = standing(threads[sid])
+            std = standard_terms(threads[sid])
+            if offer and must_haves_ok(case, terms, std):
+                cost = max(self.costs(case, sid, terms, std))
+                if cost <= alternative:
+                    candidates.append((cost, sid, offer))
+        if candidates:
+            _, sid, offer = min(candidates)
+            return {"supplier_id": sid, "message": {"action": {"type": "accept", "term_sheet_id": offer}}}
+        return {"supplier_id": live_threads(threads)[0], "message": {"action": {"type": "walk_away"}}}
+
+    def decide(self, case, threads):
+        record = {"decision": len(self.decisions) + 1, "fallback": False}
+        try:
+            if self.disabled:
+                raise ValueError("Model disabled after previous error")
+            state = {}
+            for sid in live_threads(threads):
+                offer, terms = standing(threads[sid])
+                std = standard_terms(threads[sid])
+                state[sid] = {"offer_id": offer, "terms": terms, "standard_terms": std,
+                              "estimated_cost_scenarios": self.costs(case, sid, terms, std),
+                              "history": threads[sid]}
+            user = self.brief + "\nLIVE STATE (cost estimates use 12% supplier financing, cost +/-5%):\n" + encoded(state)
+            raw = self.model.complete(self.system, user)
+            record["model_output"] = raw
+            proposal = parse(raw)
+            body = str(proposal.get("body", ""))
+            known_offers = {standing(events)[0] for events in threads.values()}
+            if any(not self.fact(case, ref) and ref not in known_offers for ref in ID_RE.findall(body)):
+                raise ValueError("Model cited unknown evidence")
+            decision = self.guard(case, threads, proposal)
+            if not decision:
+                raise ValueError("Invalid model decision")
+            msg = decision["message"]
+            if (msg.get("action") or {}).get("type") == "accept":
+                # One-supplier pilot: safe_close adds conservative relationship-cost evaluation.
+                safe = self.safe_close(case, threads)
+                if safe != decision:
+                    raise ValueError("Acceptance failed conservative cost check")
+            for sheet in msg.get("term_sheets", []):
+                price = sheet["terms"].get("unit_price")
+                if not isinstance(price, (int, float)) or not math.isfinite(price) or price <= 0:
+                    raise ValueError("Invalid unit price")
+                if not must_haves_ok(case, sheet["terms"]):
+                    raise ValueError("Proposed terms violate must-haves")
+            record["executed"] = decision
+        except Exception as exc:
+            self.disabled = True
+            decision = self.safe_close(case, threads)
+            record.update(fallback=True, reason=str(exc), executed=decision)
+        self.decisions.append(record)
+        (self.folder / "decisions.json").write_text(json.dumps(self.decisions, indent=2) + "\n")
+        print(f"Decision {len(self.decisions)}: {'fallback' if record['fallback'] else 'LLM'}", flush=True)
+        return decision
+
+
+class RecordingTable(RemoteTable):
+    def __init__(self, client, folder):
+        super().__init__(client)
+        self.folder, self.messages = folder, []
+
+    def record(self, who, sid, message):
+        self.messages.append({"who": who, "supplier_id": sid, "message": message})
+        (self.folder / "conversation.json").write_text(json.dumps(self.messages, indent=2) + "\n")
+        lines = ["# Hosted practice conversation\n"]
+        for i, entry in enumerate(self.messages, 1):
+            msg = entry["message"]
+            lines += [f"## {i}. {entry['who']} — {entry['supplier_id']}\n", str(msg.get("body", "")),
+                      "\n```json\n" + json.dumps({k: v for k, v in msg.items() if k != "body"}, indent=2) + "\n```\n"]
+        (self.folder / "conversation.md").write_text("\n".join(lines))
+        print(f"{who} {sid}: {message.get('body', message.get('action', message.get('status', '')))}", flush=True)
+
+    def open(self, case_id):
+        case, threads = super().open(case_id)
+        (self.folder / "session.json").write_text(json.dumps({"session_id": self.session_id, "case_id": case_id}))
+        for sid, messages in threads.items():
+            for message in messages:
+                self.record("Supplier", sid, message)
+        return case, threads
+
+    def send(self, supplier_id, message):
+        self.record("Buyer (submitted)", supplier_id, message)
+        reply = super().send(supplier_id, message)
+        self.record("Supplier", supplier_id, reply)
+        return reply
+
+    def close(self, supplier_id, message):
+        self.record("Buyer (submitted)", supplier_id, message)
+        result = super().close(supplier_id, message)
+        self.record("Result", supplier_id, result)
+        return result
+
+

+        raise ValueError("Unexpected arena URL")
+    folder = ROOT / "artifacts/live" / datetime.now(UTC).strftime("%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%fZ")

+        print(f"Artifacts: {folder}", flush=True)

+# Improving negotiation performance
+
+## What the scores mean
+
+P01 adaptive previously averaged 61.78/100 over two runs; P03 scored 85.15 in one run. These are normalized savings against each case's hidden best package, not deal success rates. All three closed valid deals. Near 100 requires extracting almost all available total-cost improvement; a bigger context window or a stronger-sounding prompt does not establish that the supplier will accept the requested package. The hidden benchmark is for post-run evaluation, never a live input.
+
+## Findings from our code and saved runs
+
+1. **Counteroffers lacked calculated comparisons.** The original LiveAgent supplies costs for the standing offer, but asks the model to invent its own packages. A P01 reciprocal-trades run accepted EUR 137.50 with 14-day payment and incurred EUR 11,455.28 in buyer financing cost. The concession did not compensate for the payment trade.
+2. **True evidence can support the seller.** Adaptive cited an increasing PPI-C241 index; the supplier explicitly replied that it confirmed its cost case. All claims being verified is a reliability metric, not proof of persuasion.
+3. **Retrieval can omit the useful comparison window.** Dossiers are capped at 40,000 JSON characters in live runs. P01 omitted 634 records; P03 omitted 536. Recent recorded model inputs were about 14,500–15,700 tokens, without evidence of overflow. The P01 index card used July–August 2026, even though the full public data includes a twelve-month energy decline: PPI-D351 137.0 in August 2025 to 131.9 in August 2026 (-3.72%). The supplier's labor and material indices increased over their respective twelve-month windows. Any argument must state its own window and cost share; an energy decline does not prove total costs declined.
+4. **Supplier-specific notes are already available but weakly operationalized.** P01 notes describe outdated cost spreadsheets, a preference for faster payment and remembered help during 2022. P03 notes describe pricing-committee approval above 2%, a price freeze and flexibility on other terms. These are contextual clues, not exact hidden reservation prices or guarantees of concessions.
+5. **Supplier-health estimates are uncertain.** We currently assume 12% supplier financing and a central should-cost estimate. The +/-5% scenarios can change package rankings. Optimizing that estimate too confidently may optimize the wrong objective; a disclosed cost breakdown could improve it.
+6. **Communication is deliberately restricted.** The model chooses tone, intent, fact cards and terms; code writes the message. This prevents invented numeric claims but cannot yet express all relationship acknowledgments or nuanced conditional trades. Expanding safe message choices is a separate experiment.
+
+## Implemented experimental improvement
+
+`nighthunter/economics.py` enumerates up to 512 permitted non-price combinations and a price grid from 90% to 100% of the standing price in 0.25% increments. It reuses upstream total-cost arithmetic, respects must-haves, calculates financing/coverage/quality/estimated relationship effects, and returns at most eight distinct payment/date/security packages. Each candidate includes estimated total cost, cost components, cost at the current unit price and uncertainty scenarios. This is a bounded request menu, not a global optimizer or acceptance forecast.
+
+The advisor also rebuilds a within-session memory from supplier offers: concessions in estimated total cost, stagnation, status and messages left. It excludes buyer anchors from observed supplier concessions. It reads only the supplied dossier and the current thread, not practice results, hidden floors or final endpoints.
+
+Enable it with `--variant adaptive --policy economics`. The default remains `--policy current`. The additional instructions are in `prompts/economics_policy.md`; `prompts/common.md` and the four original variant files are unchanged. The new policy encourages calculated trades, relevant evidence, approval requests when appropriate and measured continuation while the supplier remains open. Existing evidence validation, acceptance checks and budget limits remain in force.
+
+This changes both the advisory input and its policy instructions, so the comparison evaluates the combined feature, not wording alone. The same model, case dossier, common rules and safeguards are frozen within a batch. Changes to retrieval, model or message rendering need separate experiments.
+
+Validation before live comparison: 34 local tests passed, including financing trade-offs, supplier/part estimate matching, supplier-only concession history, must-haves, bounded search, supplier-health penalties and independence from injected hidden-result fields. Targeted Python/import lint passes. A broader inherited Ruff ruleset also reports existing style warnings in earlier files; it was not made a new project-wide gate. Candidate construction on saved P01/P03 openings took roughly 6–18 ms locally.
+
+## Examples worth building on
+
+| Source | What to reuse |
+|---|---|
+| [Starter README: Haggler example](../vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/README.md) | `decide(case, threads)`, cost the counteroffer, ask for a breakdown, explicitly accept. It is a demonstration, not a competitive strategy. |
+| [NaiveAgent](../vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/naive.py) | Simple anchor, split the gap, close on final/agreed; regression baseline. |
+| [LLMAgent](../vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/agents/llm.py) | Current offers, attached document text, model adapter and closing guard. |
+| [Cost helpers](../vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/cost.py) | Total cost, supplier cash value, supplier-health penalty and fixed-horizon coverage. |
+| [Document readers](../vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/arena_kit/docs.py) | Quote defaults and PDF/XLSX text. XLSX formulas are returned as text, not evaluated. |
+| [API evidence and document rules](../vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/brief/api.md) | Applicable claim windows, verified versus persuasive evidence, approval and breakdown requests. |
+
+There is no winning trained agent or hosted supplier implementation in this snapshot. Local simulator scores test the API contract, not realistic negotiation skill.
+
+## How the agent should learn
+
+**Within a negotiation (initial version implemented):** read replies, preserve exact standing offers and constraints, update concession history, compare packages and adapt the next request. A stalled trajectory is an observation, not proof of a hard floor. Structured memory makes the information easier to use; it does not train model weights.
+
+**Between practice runs (controlled development loop):** save outcomes and traces → identify a repeated failure → write one general hypothesis → change one feature → run paired comparisons → keep or reject the change. Record failures, not only best leaderboard scores. Preserve case families not used for tuning. Do not put previous `c_best`, hidden outcome values or post-session traces into the live negotiator's context. We have not implemented automatic prompt rewriting, weight training or a cross-run learning database.
+
+## Next experiments, in order
+
+1. Finish the economic-policy comparison on P01, then check P03 before promoting it. Use matched repeats; require valid autonomous completion and no increased failure rate as well as better scores.

+3. Model supplier priorities explicitly: source-linked cash/approval/relationship hypotheses, uncertainty and latest observations. Ask for a breakdown when useful, parse disclosed values deterministically and retain their provenance. Do not infer undisclosed actual cost from an estimate.
+4. Test richer validated messages: acknowledgments grounded in notes, conditional payment-for-price trades and approval escalation. Keep numerical statements templated and claims checked.
+5. Evaluate adaptive and evidence-first across more case types with repeated paired runs. Add RFQ scheduling and final-wave deadlines before claiming broad readiness. Only then test a different model on difficult decisions as a separate budgeted comparison.
+
+Retain the USD 5 cumulative ledger and preserve practice quota. A failed hypothesis is useful evidence; do not promote it because its architecture sounds stronger. No near-100 result is promised.

content.text:
Your strategy is good **as a development loop**, with one important limit: the three bundled local suppliers follow simple scripts. Running them many times can make the agent more reliable, but a higher local score would not show that it has become a better negotiator against the hosted suppliers. The starter kit says this explicitly in its [simulator documentation](/Users/nourmaalej/NightHunter_EHL/vendor/negotiation-arena-kit/starter-kit/README.md).

I’d run the loop this way:

1. **After each change, test locally** for valid offers, correct cost calculations, citations, timing, and autonomous closure. Use saved discussions to spot recurring mistakes and form one improvement hypothesis at a time.
2. **Test that change on hosted practice cases**, comparing it with the previous version on the *same cases*, model, dossier, and safeguards. Keep every run, including failures, in the results.
3. **Rotate across case types.** We have hosted evidence only for P01 and P03; P02 and the other practice cases are still gaps. A policy that helps P01 but hurts P02 should not become the default.
4. **Reserve cases for validation.** Once we use a case’s replay to revise the prompt, it becomes a development case. Check the resulting version on other cases it has not been tailored to.

“Learning” here means improving our prompt, code, and within-session memory from observed failures; the model’s weights are not being trained. We should judge progress by **average score per case, worst-case score, deal completion, and failures**, rather than the best replay alone. Our [saved-run review](/Users/nourmaalej/NightHunter_EHL/docs/SAVED_RUN_REVIEW.md) shows why: even repeated P01 runs with the same policy varied substantially.

My next priority would be the small input fix already identified—unused evidence cards and a clear offer history—then a controlled P01/P03 comparison, followed by a first P02 hosted test. Before claiming good coverage across *all* cases, we also need to handle RFQs with multiple suppliers; the current live runner supports one supplier. Near 100 on every case is an ambition, not something local repetition can guarantee.
